# Standards

Variant: base · Rules: 18 (core 13, design 5, variant 0)

Cite a rule as `path:line [rule.id]`.

## Goals

- A minimal Expo template for English-only iOS and Android MVPs that AI coding agents extend safely.
- Production-ready auth on two variant branches (Supabase and Firebase): Google sign-in on both platforms, Sign in with Apple on iOS.
- One brand look with platform-correct behaviour on iOS and Android.
- Anything that can be checked by a script is checked by a script; only judgement stays as prose.
- Works from Windows, Linux and macOS, with bun only and TypeScript only.
- Production bar: a change is done when the local checks pass, both platforms were exercised, and nothing is called working from reading code alone.

## Non-goals

- Server code in the template
- CI
- Expo Go
- Web, tablet or landscape-first layouts
- App Check in core
- Certificate pinning
- Jailbreak detection
- A profiles table or any user data model
- Apple sign-in on Android
- A third auth provider as a branch

## Rules

### auth.apple-with-google

Where Google sign-in is offered on iOS, Sign in with Apple is offered too.

- Why: App Store guideline 4.8 requires an equivalent privacy-focused login next to any third-party login.
- Enforced by: agent: mobile-security-auditor

### auth.nonce

Every ID-token sign-in uses a fresh nonce: the hashed nonce goes to the identity provider, the raw nonce to the backend, and a cached token is never sent to a backend.

- Why: A cached token carries no fresh nonce, so a replayed token would pass the backend check.
- Enforced by: agent: mobile-security-auditor

### backport.criteria

A feature backported from a production app must be generic, tested and inside the template's scope.

- Why: The template stays reusable and minimal. App-specific code does not belong in it, and a human decides what is generic.
- Enforced by: agent: adversarial-reviewer

### core.minimal-abstraction

Write the simplest code that works: no new layer, wrapper, option or abstraction until a second real use needs it.

- Why: Agents over-build. Every abstraction is code to review, test and keep, so delete before adding.
- Enforced by: agent: slop-reviewer

### core.no-real-config

Only example env and config files are committed; real config is gitignored and lives locally or in EAS.

- Why: Committed Firebase, Google or Supabase config leaks project identifiers and invites committed secrets. Each app and each environment has its own values. No script can tell a real config file from an example, so the reviewer of every diff checks it; secrets:check only catches key formats with a known prefix.
- Enforced by: agent: adversarial-reviewer

### core.no-server-code

The template ships no server code: no Edge Functions, Cloud Functions or backend services.

- Why: A template with a server forces every app onto one backend and one deployment story. Server pieces ship as pattern docs.
- Enforced by: agent: adversarial-reviewer

### core.pattern-not-code

Optional features ship as pattern docs, not as code in the template.

- Why: Core stays minimal and every line in it is tested. A pattern is applied only when an app picks it.
- Enforced by: agent: new-feature

### core.public-env-only

Only publishable values go under EXPO_PUBLIC_*; anything else is a secret and never enters the JS bundle.

- Why: EXPO_PUBLIC_* values are inlined into the bundle and readable in both the iOS and the Android binary.
- Enforced by: agent: adversarial-reviewer

### core.tokens-in-keychain

Tokens and credentials are kept in expo-secure-store, or in storage encrypted with a key that lives there; never in plain MMKV, AsyncStorage or logs.

- Why: Plain app storage is readable from device backups and on rooted devices; Keychain and Keystore are hardware-backed where the device has it.
- Enforced by: agent: mobile-security-auditor

### core.typescript-only

Source, scripts, hooks and configs are TypeScript. The only .js files are `jest.config.js` (Jest 29 loads a TypeScript config through ts-node, which is not a dependency, and that fails under verbatimModuleSyntax) and `metro.config.js` (Metro loads its config through Node, which reads TypeScript only from version 22.18 on while engines allows 22.12, and it cannot resolve expo/metro-config from an ES module). No .mjs, .cjs, .jsx or .sh files.

- Why: One language for the app, the tooling and the agents; Windows-safe; type-checked.
- Enforced by: script: docs:check

### design.contrast

Every token pair meets WCAG AA in both themes (text 4.5:1, icons and outlines 3:1), including placeholder, pressed fills, solid fills under the Android ripple and icon glyphs; every colour token exists in light and dark. Disabled text is exempt, and so are the documented transient pressed states (see the design-system skill).

- Why: Fading a white-on-blue button for its iOS pressed state drops it from 5.17:1 to 3.62:1; a token missing from one theme renders as nothing in it.
- Enforced by: script: contrast:check

### design.font-scaling

Never allowFontScaling={false} and never adjustsFontSizeToFit on labels. Text caps scaling per role instead.

- Why: Shrinking or freezing text locks out Dynamic Type AX users and Android users at 200%; HIG says reflow, don't shrink.
- Enforced by: script: lint

### design.testids

Interactive elements have a testID in kebab-case (<screen>-<element>).

- Why: E2E tests and agents select by testID; label text is unreliable in React Native and differs per platform.
- Enforced by: script: lint

### design.tokens-only

No hex or rgb() colours, Tailwind palette classes, arbitrary [..] values, or hard-coded fontSize/fontFamily in src/. Use semantic tokens (bg-primary, text-muted) and Text variants.

- Why: A literal colour has no dark-mode value and skips contrast:check; an arbitrary value escapes the type scale and spacing.
- Enforced by: script: lint

### design.ui-primitives

No raw Pressable, Text, TextInput, Button, TouchableOpacity, TouchableHighlight or TouchableWithoutFeedback from react-native outside src/components/ui; the UI kit imports only from @/lib and its own folder.

- Why: The kit owns tokens, testIDs, accessibility and the platform press feedback; a raw primitive skips all of them, and kit imports of stores or services make it unshareable.
- Enforced by: script: lint

### intake.audit-record

No dependency is added without an approved intake record covering licence, maintenance, adoption, source read, provenance, Expo SDK and New Architecture compatibility, native impact and migration cost.

- Why: A dependency is code we ship and cannot read in full. The record makes the choice reviewable, and a human approves it before anything is installed.
- Enforced by: agent: research

### intake.pin-risky-native

A native package with a bus factor of one, or a version below 1.0, is pinned to an exact version.

- Why: A native module breaks the build, not just the app. A caret range lets an unreviewed release in.
- Enforced by: agent: research

### release.r8-e2e

After a native change, re-run the Android release (R8) e2e before shipping.

- Why: R8 minification can strip or rename classes that a debug build keeps, and only a release build shows it.
- Enforced by: human
